Friday, 6th December, 2013/15th Agrahayana, 1935 (Saka)
The House met at eleven of the clock,
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair.

OBITUARY REFERENCE
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing
away of Mr. Nelson Mandela, former President of South Africa and one of the greatest
personalities of our times, who represented the best of human spirit and values.
As an anti-apartheid revolutionary, he was convicted and sentenced to life
imprisonment in 1964 and was released in 1990, after 27 years. Inspired by Mahatma
Gandhi in his long walk and struggle against apartheid, he along with other leaders
organised mass boycotts especially against the laws supporting racial discrimination and
oppression including the Representation of V oters Act and Prohibition of Mixed
Marriages Act.
In January 1995, we had the privilege of being addressed by Mr. Mandela in
Parliament and on that occasion while recalling the strong bonds of history and geography
uniting both our nations, he said:
"It is a history of shared commitment to freedom and democracy, to non-racialism
and tolerance, to social equity and the eradication of poverty. It is a history of
common experience of oppression and struggle for independence and freedom. It
is a history of interdependence in struggle and mutual support."
India bestowed upon him the Bharat Ratna in 1990. He was also the recipient of
the UNESCO Peace Prize in 1991, the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993, Indira Gandhi Award
for International Justice and Harmony in 1996.
Mr. Mandela was a living symbol of his people's quest for freedom and dignity
against tyranny and injustice. While his courage, determination and sacrifice inspired
millions of people during the anti-apartheid movement, his message of peace, forgiveness
and reconciliation thereafter, united them and led the rainbow nation on the path to
peace and progress.

Obituary Reference
In the passing away of Mr. Nelson Mandela, the South African people have lost
the father of their nation and the world a statesman, whose life and message of courage
and goodness would continue to inspire and guide all of us around the world in the
years ahead.
We deeply mourn the passing away of Mr. Nelson Mandela.
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect
to the memory of the departed leader.
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
MR. CHAIRMAN: As a mark of respect to the memory of Mr. Nelson Mandela,
the House stands adjourned till 11.00 
AM on Monday, the 9th of December, 2013.
The House then adjourned at four minutes past eleven of the clock till eleven
of the clock on Monday, the 9th December, 2013.
